title: Console MVP surface paring: narrow dashboards, trace sampling, and coarse cost breakdown
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context: The full observability PRD contains a wide set of dashboard tiles, token-level cost breakdowns, request-level trace aggregation, and long retention windows. Given time and engineering constraints for the March release we need a focused MVP that delivers actionable visibility while keeping build scope small and predictable. This ticket defines the scope reductions, the rationale, and acceptance criteria for the trimmed Console observability surface. Goal: ship a usable observability set that helps engineers and platform owners diagnose regressions and cost spikes without the full fidelity features that would push the release past the cycle.

Scope cuts proposed (MVP):
- Dashboards: ship 6 tiles (throughput, p50/p95 latency, error rate, model-utilization summary, request rate by route, active model variants). Drop: per-tenant heatmaps, full time-series breakdown per route, and custom card builder for MVP.
- Tracing: only surface sampled traces for requests above the p95 latency threshold (configurable sample rate). Drop: full distributed trace capture for every request and per-span timelines in MVP.
- Cost breakdown: provide coarse-grained cost buckets by model family (open vs. quantized vs. hosted) and route groups (ingest, chat, batch). Drop: token-level and call-level chargeback for MVP; provide CSV export of raw cost events for early adopters.
- Retention: metrics + traces retained for 7 days in the UI (baseline). Drop longer retention tiers from GA scope; customers will be able to request extended retention as an enterprise feature post-MVP.
- Instrumentation: include lightweight tracing hooks and aggregated sampling counters to ensure metrics are consistent. Avoid heavy prefix/KV caching instrumentation for now.

Rationale: These cuts preserve the core developer needs (latency, throughput, errors, and coarse cost signal) while keeping engineering effort focused on stable APIs, reliable sampling, and clear alerting paths. They intentionally trade fidelity for delivery speed and deterministic resource cost for Redwood.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows the six dashboard tiles defined in scope for all customers in the canary org by release date.
Traces surface for requests that exceed configured p95 latency threshold with minimum contextual fields: request id, route, model variant, timestamp, and latency.
Cost view shows aggregated cost by model family and route group and supports CSV export of raw cost events for billing reconciliation.
Retention: metrics and sampled traces are viewable in the UI for at least 7 days; queries against 7-day window return within SLA (2s for dashboard tiles).
Feature-flag gating present: "console.observability.mvp" flag controls visibility and defaults to off for customers outside canary org.
On-call runbook updated with two playbooks: diagnosing a dashboard regression and investigating unexpected cost bucket increases.
End-to-end test coverage exists for dashboard rendering, sampling behavior, and cost CSV export (smoke tests pass in CI).
decision_rationale: We prioritized developer-facing signal that reduces mean time to detect regressions (latency and error spikes) and gives product teams early cost visibility without building full chargeback. Sampling traces on p95 keeps trace storage bounded and focuses developer attention on the likely problematic requests. Coarse cost buckets enable immediate triage while deferring complex chargeback and token-level views to post-MVP enterprise work.
implementation_notes: Backend: reuse existing metrics ingestion pipeline; add a sampling filter that marks high-latency requests for trace extraction (ENG-8421).

Frontend: implement compact dashboard layout and a lightweight trace viewer that links to raw event CSV. Keep styling consistent with Console tokens. (See figma: https://drive.google.com/example/mvp-dashboard).
Config: implement p95 sampling threshold with default 1000ms; surface as a settings toggle behind feature flag.
Performance: ensure dashboard tile queries complete under 2s for 7-day window — coordinate with infra team to provision query index or cache (dependency ENG-9173).
review_feedback: Design review 2026-03-02: asked to reduce initial tile count to 6 to minimize layout complexity; approved with the compact grid approach.
Security review 2026-03-04: confirmed no additional PII is surfaced in MVP traces; no KMS changes required for 7-day retention.
Sales/dev-rel feedback 2026-03-06: request for CSV export for early finance reconciliation; agreed as MVP compromise.
Engineering note 2026-03-08: suggested increasing default p95 threshold to 1200ms to avoid noisy traces on low-throughput tenants; accepted and made configurable.
updates: 2026-03-03 — Scoping session: cut custom card builder and per-tenant heatmaps; moved to post-MVP backlog.
2026-03-05 — Backend spike complete: sampling hook implemented in metrics pipeline (prototype).
2026-03-07 — Design handoff: Figma frames linked and compact tile styles approved.
2026-03-09 — QA: initial smoke tests for CSV export failing due to timestamp timezone mismatch; ENG assigned to fix (ENG-9173).
2026-03-10 — Ready for review: acceptance criteria updated with SLA numbers and runbook tasks.
